exemptions: Certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; housing under stricter local rent control; some single-family homes owned by individuals

interaction.note: Does not apply to housing under local rent control that is stricter (§ 1947.12(d)(3)).

what_next.label: Read the law on the California Legislature site

title: California just-cause eviction rule
summary: After 12 months, a landlord needs a listed reason to end the tenancy and must state it in writing.
key_value: Just cause after 12 months; one month's rent relocation for no-fault
coverage_in_words: Most rental housing in California after 12 months of tenancy. Not for housing with a certificate of occupancy in the last 15 years, and not where a local just-cause ordinance applies.
exemptions: Certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years; owner-occupied single-family and duplex cases; property under a local just-cause ordinance

interaction.note: Where a local just-cause ordinance applies, the local ordinance applies instead (§ 1946.2(i)).

eviction.reasons: At-fault reasons (e.g. non-payment, material lease breach) and no-fault reasons (e.g. owner move-in, withdrawal from the market, substantial remodel).
eviction.notice: Written notice stating the just cause. A curable violation first needs a notice to correct it, then a three-day notice to quit.
eviction.relocation: No-fault: one month's rent (as relocation money or a waived final month), paid within 15 days of the notice.
